xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs: As part of the income tax assessment, it was observed that there is a difference in capital gain computation for the property sold during the year 2012-13. The Income Tax Department has referred the same to the valuation officer. Giving effect petition had been filed. The Quantum of claims amounts to Rs. 1.05 crores (including interest)
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:CurrentStatusOfTheLitigationOr: Considering the merits of the case, the company has opted to settle the dispute through Vivad Se Vishwas scheme 2025. The relevant form for opting the scheme , Form 1 has been filed. The company is awaiting for the reply of the Assessing officer in response to the same.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheOpposingParty: The Hon'ble Commissioner of Customs, Chennai
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs: The Company imports thermal line printers from one of our neighboring countries (Duty Free). There is a difference in the opinion between the Company and the Customs department on classification of such imported goods for determination of Customs Duty. The Company contested the same. The Company had received an order from the office of the Commissioner of Customs (Audit), Chennai, dated 6th December 2023 to pay Rs.35.58 Crores (including differential duty of Rs.10.02 Cr and fines/penalties on the Company, its Customs House Agent, Company Secretary and other official)
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:CurrentStatusOfTheLitigationOr: The Company has filed appeal before the CESTAT. The hearing is posted on 29.01.2026. Awaiting further communication.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs: GST Assessment Order received U/s.73 on 23/12/2023 with demand raised by the department for the year 2017-18 on Input tax Credit (ITC) related to credit notes and other ITC. The Company filed detailed reply along with supporting documents to the department. The quantum of claims amount to Rs. 17.04 crores.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:CurrentStatusOfTheLitigationOr: The Comany has filed an appeal before the Joint Commissioner- State Tax- New Delhi. Awaiting further communication.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheOpposingParty: Sr. Joint Commissioner of Revenue, Kolkata South Circle
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs: GST Assessment Order dated 29th April 2024 received U/s.73 with demand raised by the department for the year 2018-19 on tax paid in short against outward and Input tax Credit (ITC) claimed in excess. Expected financial implications amount to 69.83 lakhs (including Interest and Penalty of Rs. 35.46 lakhs)
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:CurrentStatusOfTheLitigationOr: The Company has filed appeal with Special Commissioner of Revenue, Appellate Authority and received demand order for ₹77.79 Lakhs (including interest and penalty of ₹ 45.37 Lakhs). The Company is in the process of filing appeal with Appellate Tribunal.
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:NameOfTheOpposingParty: Office of Deputy Commissioner of State Tax (SGST), Gurugram (East),Haryana
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:StatusOfTheLitigationDisputeAs: Issued Show Cause Notice u/s 73(1) of HGST/CGST Act 2017 with demand for the year 2020-21 on Input tax Credit (ITC) claimed in excess. The expected financial implications amount to Rs. 73.20 Lakhs (Including Interest and Penalty of 32.93 Lakhs).
xbrli:xbrl.in-capmkt:CurrentStatusOfTheLitigationOr: Considering the reply of the Company, the demand amount has been reduced from Rs. 73.20 Lakhs (Including Interest and Penalty) to Rs. 23.12 Lakhs (Including Interest and Penalty). The Company is in the process of filing appeal before the Excise and Taxation Officer, Gurgaon, Haryana.
